title: The Best Freshsales Alternatives in 2026: Smarter Picks by Use Case
summary: Find the best Freshsales alternative for your CRM needs in 2026. Compare automation, flexibility, pricing, and which tool is right for each use case.
body_text: TL;DR: The best Freshsales alternative in 2026 depends on your main need: Saleoid is the top pick for affordable automation, HelloGrowthCRM for built-in lead scoring, HubSpot for integrated marketing, Pipedrive for sales pipeline focus, Zoho CRM for all-in-one suite, Salesforce for deep customization, and Miniloop for teams needing custom-built workflows and 5x–significantly lower long-term costs. The Best Freshsales Alternatives in 2026: Smarter Picks by Use Case Last updated: August 2026 The top freshsales alternative are Saleoid (advanced automation for small teams), HelloGrowthCRM (lead scoring & insights in every plan), HubSpot (marketing automation leader), Pipedrive (sales pipeline management), Zoho CRM (comprehensive sales and marketing suite), Salesforce (full-scale customization & integrations), Miniloop (custom CRM workflows, no per-seat fees). More businesses are re-evaluating Freshsales as automation needs and CRM costs rise. In 2026, alternatives have matured, offering everything from advanced automation at entry-level prices (Saleoid) to customizable CRM builds (Miniloop). Teams with unique workflows or large user counts are prioritizing long-term savings, automation flexibility, and data ownership. The market now splits between out-of-the-box tools and those built for total process control. Why people look for Freshsales alternatives Freshsales still appeals on usability and common workflows. But it restricts advanced automation and integration capabilities to higher-priced tiers, so many growing teams hit limits fast. Cost-conscious businesses see long-term complexity and ballooning per-seat fees as roadblocks, while teams with unusual processes face workarounds or unsupported needs. As a result, organizations are looking elsewhere: some want affordable automation at every level, others require data control and CRM flexibility. This is where Freshsales competitors offer stronger value for specialized use cases. Comparison table: Freshsales alternatives at a glance For teams sizing up Freshsales alternatives, the main differentiators are automation strength at entry tier, depth of sales or marketing automation, customization, and the types of businesses each CRM best serves. Some tools prioritize plug-and-play simplicity or affordable automation, while others, like Salesforce, stand out for intricate customization. The table below captures the core value, automation approach, and ideal fit for each major Freshsales alternative. Use it for a fast side-by-side snapshot. Tool Best Use Case Automation Depth Customization/Flexibility Ideal Buyer Saleoid Affordable workflow automation Advanced, even at entry tiers Moderate; templates and some flexible setups SMBs and startups looking for high automation without high costs HelloGrowthCRM Built-in AI lead scoring AI insights in all plans Limited to standard workflows Teams needing lead scoring and sales insights out of the box HubSpot Marketing automation Strong at higher tiers Modular, but customization can get expensive Teams prioritizing marketing features and integrations Pipedrive Streamlined sales pipeline management Basic automation Focused, but less customizable Sales teams wanting visual pipelines and simple workflows Zoho CRM All-in-one suite Broad automation tools Highly customizable for mid-market Businesses needing an integrated platform for sales and marketing Salesforce Deep customization, enterprise scale Powerful, advanced automation Maximum. Full custom objects, fields, and integrations Enterprises and process-heavy teams with complex needs Miniloop Custom workflows + long-term CRM cost reduction Tailored per client requirements Fully bespoke. Built to your process Businesses with large CRM spends wanting data ownership and total workflow control This table lets you quickly match each CRM to your use case, whether you need AI-driven lead scoring, affordable all-in-one workflows, enterprise-level customization, or a solution custom-built around your exact requirements. For more on how the boundaries between automation and workflow ownership are evolving, see our breakdown in Best Clay Alternatives in 2026: Tools That Go Beyond Data Enrichment . For affordable automation: Saleoid Saleoid stands out as the best Freshsales alternative for teams seeking advanced automation at a budget-friendly price. Unlike Freshsales, which restricts its most powerful workflow automation tools to higher-tier plans, Saleoid includes robust sales, marketing, and billing automation even in its lowest priced tiers. That makes it a go-to for small businesses and startups that want to automate repetitive tasks and scale activity without breaking the bank. The advantage comes from eliminating typical feature gating. Entry-level Saleoid subscribers gain access to sophisticated workflow automation that usually requires upgrading with other vendors. This means small teams can build end-to-end sales pipelines, automate client onboarding, trigger communications based on lead status, and link marketing and billing flows. All without bumping up against artificial plan limits. It directly addresses the pain point many face with Freshsales: needing to pay for higher-priced plans just to enable automation that fits modern selling. Saleoid’s focus on affordable automation is best suited for organizations where speed and process efficiency matter more than niche integrations or granular reporting. For a team aiming to maximize productivity with minimal manual effort, such as a small sales agency or early-stage SaaS, Saleoid’s workflow engine is a clear upgrade over Freshsales’ limited entry plans. Teams facing similar automation tradeoffs can also explore broader process automation options, like those discussed in our n8n pricing guide , to further control costs and optimize their stack. Ditch your expensive CRM subscription Get a custom CRM designed for your workflow at a fraction of the price. Talk to our team to get a fixed quote. Book a call For built-in lead scoring: HelloGrowthCRM HelloGrowthCRM stands out as the top Freshsales alternative for outbound teams that want native AI lead scoring and sales insights included, rather than hidden behind premium tiers or expensive add-ons. Every HelloGrowthCRM plan comes standard with AI lead scoring, automated call summaries, and sales insights, making it a go-to choice for data-driven sales operations that rely on actionable intelligence right out of the box. Best for: Outbound teams needing robust, built-in lead scoring and real-time sales insights Key features: AI-driven lead scoring included by default Automated call summaries for each interaction Sales insights and reports in every pricing tier Streamlined integration with dialers and email tools Activity and engagement tracking Simplified, user-friendly dashboard Pricing: Custom pricing. Request a quote Strengths: Consistent access to core sales intelligence features on every plan means teams won’t hit paywalls for crucial AI scoring or reporting as they scale. The inclusion of call summaries helps reps quickly review and prioritize leads. Weaknesses: Custom pricing may create uncertainty for budget-sensitive teams, and the platform’s specialization means it isn’t a fit for companies seeking a broader marketing automation or pipeline management suite. Choose HelloGrowthCRM when: You want sales insights, lead scoring, and AI-driven call summaries as standard features rather than premium upgrades, and your team cares most about actionable outbound sales intelligence. For marketing automation: HubSpot For teams that need comprehensive marketing automation, HubSpot stands out as a clear upgrade over Freshsales. HubSpot is highly regarded for delivering an all-in-one CRM experience that covers email marketing, campaign management, nurturing workflows, and robust lead tracking in a single, cohesive platform. Its automation capabilities are built into virtually every tier, making it an ideal choice for businesses driven by content and inbound marketing strategies that require reliable, scalable automation. HubSpot sets itself apart with a vast ecosystem of integrations, connecting to countless third-party tools and platforms. Useful for marketing teams that rely on a diverse tech stack. The user interface is designed for accessibility, enabling marketers to build complex automation sequences or set up lead scoring rules with minimal friction. This combination of power and approachability supports businesses looking to orchestrate multi-channel campaigns without technical debt or long onboarding times. For teams whose growth relies on publishing, tracking, and converting inbound leads, HubSpot's automation toolkit is notably more mature than those found in most “sales-first” CRMs. Its reporting and analytics dashboards enable tight feedback loops across campaigns, which is essential for optimizing spend and content strategy. Paired with its content publishing tools and extensive support resources, HubSpot provides a marketing-centric workflow that requires little compromise or workaround to scale. For thorough reviews of solutions in adjacent spaces, see our in-depth looks at Hunter.io and CIENCE , both of which address data enrichment and outbound prospecting use cases. For sales pipeline focus: Pipedrive Pipedrive stands out as the go-to Freshsales alternative for teams that prize visual sales pipeline management and a focused deal-closing workflow. Its strength is simplicity: Pipedrive is purpose-built to help sales reps track, advance, and win deals. With minimal set-up or feature overload for tasks outside the sales funnel. For organizations where the key bottleneck is coordinating opportunities and moving leads to close, Pipedrive provides a laser-focused user interface that prioritizes pipeline visibility over an array of marketing or billing automations. Pipedrive’s main appeal lies in its drag-and-drop pipeline, customizable deal stages, and lightweight onboarding. Teams can create multiple pipelines, tailor activity reminders, and set up deal rotting alerts without wading through bloat designed for marketing or operations teams. The platform deliberately avoids complex, multi-department features that can bog down process-focused sellers. In practice, this clarity means new sales reps ramp quickly, and managers always have an at-a-glance view of revenue projections and deal flow. However, teams needing deep automation, advanced lead scoring, or built-in marketing tools may find Pipedrive lacking compared to options like Saleoid or HubSpot. Still, for sales-led teams ready to move away from Freshsales and keep all attention on pipeline movement, not peripheral tasks, Pipedrive remains a top contender. For further reading on tech stacks that specialize in outbound sales workflows, consider our Orum alternatives roundup . For all-in-one suite: Zoho CRM Zoho CRM stands out as the top choice for organizations looking to consolidate their sales and marketing operations within a single platform. Zoho CRM combines a comprehensive range of automation tools, robust analytics, and deep integration capabilities, making it ideal for teams that want the convenience of managing the entire customer lifecycle without juggling multiple vendors or subscriptions. The platform offers an impressive breadth of automation features across lead management, pipeline tracking, workflow customization, and multi-channel communication. Zoho CRM is built to scale, supporting companies from startups with modest sales needs to large enterprises with complex, multi-team structures. Its flexible modules allow organizations to automate tasks from marketing campaigns to post-sale support, all while maintaining a unified view of customer relationships. For businesses prioritizing all-in-one efficiency, Zoho CRM’s ecosystem covers everything from email campaigns and AI sales assistant tools to detailed reporting and process automation. This makes it especially appealing for teams aiming to reduce software sprawl or unify fragmented workflows. However, users should be aware that the sheer variety of features can introduce complexity. Initial setup and ongoing administration may require a dedicated owner to maximize value. Zoho CRM hits the sweet spot for companies seeking a platform that can keep pace as they grow and unify operations under one roof. For deep customization: Salesforce Salesforce stands out as the CRM of choice for enterprises demanding industry-leading customization, deep integrations, and precise control over every workflow. Businesses with highly unique reporting, legacy process dependencies, or intricate approval trees consistently turn to Salesforce because it provides unmatched flexibility. Supporting everything from complex data models to granular user permissions. High upfront and ongoing costs are offset by the platform’s ability to scale and adapt to virtually any business need, making it a mainstay for organizations where ROI depends on tailoring the CRM to fit existing operations, not the other way around. Salesforce’s ecosystem includes point-and-click automation builders, an extensive AppExchange marketplace, and a mature set of APIs for connecting with internal systems or external platforms. This expansiveness allows teams to build custom dashboards, automate approvals, and support unique sales cycles. All without sacrificing performance at scale. Its reporting tools are especially robust, supporting multi-level custom objects and real-time analytics designed for decision-makers in complex environments. However, this customization power brings complexity. Implementing and maintaining Salesforce often requires specialized administrators or consulting partners, extensive user training, and ongoing investment in both configuration and platform fees. The licensing model can be expensive for organizations with large user bases or frequent workflow changes, and simple process tweaks might trigger project-level change management. For teams that outgrow the flexibility of out-of-the-box CRMs and are willing to invest in a fully tailored environment, Salesforce remains the gold standard. Its architecture enables ambitious IT and ops leaders to replicate and extend the most nuanced business processes, including those that span multiple departments or geographies, without fighting software limitations. For less resource-intensive organizations or those early in their CRM journey, however, the platform’s cost and complexity may outweigh its benefits. For custom workflows and long-term cost savings: Miniloop Miniloop [miniloop.ai] is built specifically for organizations whose workflow goes far beyond what off-the-shelf CRMs allow. Rather than relying on a generic set of pipeline templates or rigid feature sets, Miniloop delivers a custom CRM solution designed around your business’s actual processes. This isn’t a plug-and-play app; it’s a fully tailored system engineered to fit complex requirements and to evolve alongside your organization. A standout advantage for teams with many users is the fundamental break from per-seat licensing. Instead of paying extra as you grow, Miniloop’s annual cost covers custom development, dedicated ongoing support, and updates, whether you’re onboarding a handful of people or scaling across departments. This model can cut CRM expenses by 5x–significantly for large teams compared to the compounding fees typical with Freshsales or other popular platforms. Miniloop also enables true data ownership and flexibility. Clients choose managed hosting on Miniloop’s servers for simplicity or deploy the system on their own infrastructure for maximum control, meeting strict data residency or compliance needs that off-the-shelf vendors struggle with. For businesses spending $50,000 a year or more on CRM solutions, especially those with unique requirements that consistently run into limits or pricey add-ons in other tools. Miniloop stands apart as the clear choice for workflow alignment, infrastructure independence, and long-term cost efficiency. Which Freshsales alternative should you choose? For automation-driven sales and marketing teams, Saleoid is the clear pick for powerful workflows at flexible pricing. HelloGrowthCRM delivers AI lead scoring and insights for teams prioritizing prospect qualification. Pipedrive optimizes pipeline management, while Zoho CRM stands out with its comprehensive suite covering sales and marketing needs. Salesforce is right for organizations with complex integration or customization demands. For businesses spending $50,000 a year or more on CRMs and requiring full control over workflows and infrastructure, Miniloop offers customized development with measurable long-term cost savings that generic CRMs cannot match. Teams prioritizing fast onboarding and low up-front costs tend to favor generic CRMs, especially when standard sales automation and reporting are sufficient. However, when data migration, precise workflow tailoring, or infrastructure ownership matter, such as migrating away from legacy tools or integrating with unique business systems, custom solutions like Miniloop help avoid the hidden costs and rigidity of per-seat SaaS. Decision-makers facing challenges with integration, data ownership, or scaling beyond off-the-shelf limitations should scrutinize CRMs promising "all-in-one" capabilities but lacking true extensibility. Matching your final choice to core operational needs, be it automation, insights, integration, or full platform ownership, is essential to ensure the CRM doesn't become a roadblock as your team grows. Where Miniloop fits: the execution gap most alternatives leave open Most Freshsales alternatives handle the basics: contact management, predefined automations, user permissions, and surface-level reporting. Yet teams quickly run into repetitive tasks. Manually migrating legacy CRM data, tweaking workflows to fit rigid templates, managing constant change requests, recreating features that “almost” fit, and following up support tickets that drag. This execution gap means busywork persists, even when switching to a supposedly modern CRM. Miniloop addresses these blind spots by offering a custom CRM developed specifically around each client’s workflow, complete with comprehensive data migration, annual support and updates, and the ability to choose where their data is hosted. Businesses ready to move past generic templates and standard feature sets find new operational control and real cost predictability, rather than patching over limitations or paying per seat for unused functions. This approach empowers teams that have outgrown fixed SaaS offerings and need their CRM to flex with their processes, not the other way around. Freshsales continues to restrict its most advanced automation and integration features to higher-priced plans, which limits flexibility for businesses that outgrow basic capabilities. Many teams encounter rising costs due to per-seat pricing, making Freshsales less attractive as the user base expands. Additionally, organizations with unique or evolving workflows often find that Freshsales requires complicated workarounds, rather than supporting genuine customization. These factors push growing businesses to seek alternatives with more transparent pricing and configurability. How do Saleoid and Freshsales automation features actually compare? Saleoid focuses on making advanced workflow automations accessible even in its entry-level plans, so small teams can streamline repetitive sales processes without major upgrades. Freshsales, on the other hand, often reserves more powerful automation features for its premium tiers, which may present roadblocks for teams on a budget. Businesses that prioritize deep automation from the outset tend to find Saleoid offers better value and flexibility at lower costs. However, organizations with tightly integrated or highly specialized automation needs may still need to consider tools with more customization capabilities. Is Miniloop only for large organizations? Miniloop is not exclusively for large enterprises but is best suited for teams with complex CRM needs or significant CRM expenditures, typically starting from around $50,000 per year. Its value lies in tailoring workflows and infrastructure ownership, which appeals most to businesses that have outgrown off-the-shelf solutions or are seeking to cut substantial CRM costs. Smaller teams with relatively simple needs may find out-of-the-box CRMs more cost-effective. However, any organization seeking a custom, cost-controlled CRM setup without per-seat pricing can benefit from Miniloop’s approach. Do any Freshsales alternatives offer true CRM customization? Most standard Freshsales alternatives emphasize out-of-the-box features with some level of configurability, but only a few support true end-to-end customization. Salesforce is well known for its deep customization ecosystem, though it can be costly and complex. Miniloop stands apart by developing custom CRM solutions built around each client's unique workflow needs, rather than forcing teams to adapt to predefined structures. This makes Miniloop particularly suitable for organizations that require workflows and data structures tailored precisely to their processes. How do per-seat CRM fees impact growing teams? Per-seat or per-user pricing structures mean that as a business grows and adds users, CRM costs can escalate sharply. This model often forces organizations to limit CRM access or seek workarounds to control budget, which can hinder collaboration and transparency. Over time, these hidden costs become significant, especially for teams with fluctuating or expanding user bases. Many businesses are now prioritizing tools that offer flat or usage-based pricing to maintain cost predictability as they scale. Can I migrate data easily between Freshsales and other CRMs? Migrating CRM data can be a complex process, as every platform differs in terms of data structure, supported fields, and automation logic. Many Freshsales alternatives provide migration tools or professional services, but the ease of migration depends on the degree of customization and data consistency in the source system. Businesses should plan for thorough mapping and validation to ensure data integrity post-migration. Solutions like Miniloop specifically incorporate full data migration as part of their service, supporting organizations that need a robust switch. Which alternative is best for integrated marketing automation? HubSpot remains the market leader for integrated marketing automation, offering a broad suite that blends CRM, email marketing, lead nurturing, and analytics. Its ecosystem is built for marketers who want smooth campaign execution and reporting within a single platform. Zoho CRM also offers comprehensive marketing automation as part of its all-in-one approach, while other CRMs in this comparison may require third-party integrations to match this level of functionality. Choosing the right tool depends on whether deep marketing features or sales-centric workflows are the top priority. What factors drive long-term CRM cost savings? Long-term CRM cost savings come from several factors, including transparent pricing, minimizing per-seat fees, and avoiding expensive add-ons or custom development for essential features. Organizations also save by choosing platforms that fit their processes closely, reducing the need for manual workarounds and costly integrations. Infrastructure choices, such as hosting on a company's own servers, can further contain costs for some businesses. Miniloop addresses cost by eliminating per-user licensing and building only what's needed, which can substantially reduce recurring expenses for certain teams. Is there a Freshsales alternative with no per-user pricing? Most Freshsales alternatives continue to price by user or feature tier, especially in the SaaS market. Miniloop, however, offers a custom CRM solution without per-seat fees, charging based on the features and hosting model required by the client. This approach enables larger teams to avoid the spiraling costs associated with adding users to traditional CRMs. For organizations prioritizing ownership and cost control, this can be a compelling differentiator. When does it make sense to pick a custom-built CRM over out-of-the-box tools? Choosing a custom-built CRM is most appropriate for businesses with highly specific workflow, integration, or data requirements that standard solutions cannot efficiently accommodate. Organizations facing substantial per-seat charges, or those seeking greater control over their data and infrastructure, often find custom builds worthwhile. While out-of-the-box tools are excellent for rapid deployment and simplicity, custom CRMs deliver long-term savings and precise fit for complex operations. Miniloop fills this need by providing tailored CRM solutions that adapt to each client's workflow, infrastructure, and cost priorities.

title: Enovis Announces Second Quarter 2026 Results
summary: Dallas, TX, August 6, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE)—Enovis™ Corporation (“Enovis” or “the Company”) (NYSE: ENOV), an innovation-driven medical technology growth company, today announced its financial results for the second quarter ended July 3, 2026. The Company will host an investor conference call and live webcast to discuss these results today at 8:30 am ET.
body_text: Second-quarter sales growth of 3% on a reported basis, 5% organic Second-quarter Reconstructive sales growth of 8% on a reported basis, 6% organic Reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance for revenue, adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EPS, and Free Cash Flow Conversion Dallas, TX, August 6, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE)—Enovis™ Corporation (“Enovis” or “the Company”) (NYSE: ENOV), an innovation-driven medical technology growth company, today announced its financial results for the second quarter ended July 3, 2026. The Company will host an investor conference call and live webcast to discuss these results today at 8:30 am ET. Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Enovis’ second-quarter net sales of $583 million grew 3% on a reported basis and 5% on an organic basis from the same quarter in 2025. Second quarter results reflect continued execution in P&R and Recon and encouraging momentum in new product introductions. Compared to the same quarter in 2025, net sales in Recon grew 8% on a reported basis and 6% on an organic basis, and P&R declined (1)% on a reported basis and grew 3% on an organic basis. Enovis also reported a second-quarter net loss of $1 million, or 0.2% of sales, and adjusted EBITDA of $104 million, or 17.9% of sales. The Company reported a second-quarter 2026 net loss of $0.02 per share and adjusted net earnings per diluted share of $0.90. “Our second-quarter results reflect a more focused organization and a portfolio that has been meaningfully reshaped over the past several years,” said Damien McDonald, Chief Executive Officer of Enovis. “Commercial execution is improving, our innovation pipeline continues to strengthen our competitive positioning, and our teams are demonstrating agility in navigating increasingly dynamic end markets. We are encouraged by this progress but acknowledge there is more work ahead to deliver consistent durable growth, particularly as we anticipate a more dynamic macroeconomic environment in the second half. We remain focused on winning each day through continuous improvement, and disciplined execution.” 2026 Financial Outlook Enovis reaffirmed financial expectations for 2026. Revenue is expected to be in a range of $2.31-2.37 billion, which incorporates 4-6% organic revenue growth. Adjusted EBITDA is expected to be in a range of $425-435 million. The guidance ranges for revenue and adjusted EBITDA are based on current exchange rates. Full-year adjusted earnings per share is expected to be in a range of $3.52 to $3.73. Full year free cash flow conversion is expected to be 25% or higher. Conference call and Webcast Investors can access the webcast via a link on the Enovis website, www.enovis.com. For those planning to participate on the call, please dial (800) 715-9871 (U.S. callers) and (646) 307-1963 (International callers) and use conference ID 6602355. A link to a replay of the call will also be available on the Enovis website later in the day. About Enovis Enovis™ (NYSE: ENOV) is a global medical technology innovator dedicated to improving lives by developing clinically differentiated solutions that enhance patient outcomes and restore motion for life. We partner with the brightest minds in health to advance care that is smarter, personalized, and more effective, while improving operational efficiency for surgeons and clinicians around the world. Enovis solutions impact the well-being of millions of patients wherever they are on their pathway to health. Discover more about Enovis at www.enovis.com. Non-GAAP Financial Measures Enovis has provided in this press release financial information that has not been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (“non-GAAP”). These non-GAAP financial measures may include one or more of the following: adjusted net income from continuing operations (“Adjusted net income”), Adjusted net income per diluted share, Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA margin, Adjusted gross profit, and Adjusted gross profit margin. Adjusted net income and Adjusted net income per diluted share exclude net income attributable to noncontrolling interest from continuing operations, net of taxes; the effect of Loss from discontinued operations, net of taxes; restructuring charges; Medical Device Regulation (“MDR”) fees and other costs; strategic transaction costs; stock-based compensation; acquisition-related intangible asset amortization; strategic purchase of economic interest on future royalty payments; and property plant and equipment step-up depreciation; goodwill impairment charges; non-cash Other (income) expense, net; and include the tax effect of adjusted pre-tax income at applicable tax rates and other tax adjustments. Enovis also presents Adjusted net income margin, which is subject to the same adjustments as Adjusted net income. Adjusted EBITDA represents Adjusted net income excluding all Other (income) expense, net; interest, taxes, and depreciation and other amortization. Enovis presents Adjusted EBITDA margin, which is subject to the same adjustments as Adjusted EBITDA. Adjusted gross profit represents gross profit excluding depreciation step-up of acquired fixed assets and the impact of restructuring charges. Adjusted gross profit margin is subject to the same adjustments as Adjusted gross profit. Organic sales growth calculates sales growth period over period, after excluding the impact of acquisitions, divestitures, and foreign exchange rate fluctuations. Free cash flow represents cash flow from operating activities less purchases of property, plant and equipment net of proceeds from sale of certain properties. Free cash flow conversion represents free cash flow divided by adjusted net income. These non-GAAP financial measures assist Enovis management in comparing its operating performance over time because certain items may obscure underlying business trends and make comparisons of long-term performance difficult, as they are of a nature and/or size that occur with inconsistent frequency or relate to discrete restructuring plans that are fundamentally different from the ongoing productivity improvements of the Company. Enovis management also believes that presenting these measures allows investors to view its performance using the same measures that the Company uses in evaluating its financial and business performance and trends. Non-GAAP financial measures should not be considered in isolation from, or as a substitute for, financial information calculated in accordance with GAAP. Investors are encouraged to review the reconciliation of these non-GAAP measures to their most directly comparable GAAP financial measures. A reconciliation of non-GAAP financial measures presented above to GAAP results has been provided in the financial tables included in this press release. title: MicroVision Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results and Highlights Commercial Momentum Across Multiple Markets
summary: Advancing Lidar 2.0 strategy with expanding customer engagements, new product launches, strengthened leadership team, improved cash burn guidance,…...
body_text: MicroVision Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results and Highlights Commercial Momentum Across Multiple Markets August 06, 2026 4:05 PM EDT Download as PDF Related Documents Earnings Webcast Audio 10-Q Filing HTML PDF XBRL ZIP Advancing Lidar 2.0 strategy with expanding customer engagements, new product launches, strengthened leadership team, improved cash burn guidance, and growing commercial pipeline REDMOND, WA / ACCESS Newswire / August 6, 2026 / MicroVision, Inc. (NASDAQ:MVIS), a leader in advanced perception solutions for industrial, security and defense, and automotive applications, today announced its second quarter 2026 results and provided a business update highlighting continued execution of its Lidar 2.0 strategy. Key Operational Highlights Advanced the Company's Lidar 2.0 strategy , expanding MicroVision's position as a perception solutions provider serving industrial, security & defense, automotive, robotics, and autonomous aerial markets. Launched the MOVIA™ Air product family , with several pre-launch partners, introducing both MOVIA™ Air and MOVIA™ Air Plus, purpose-built airborne perception solutions designed for drones, autonomous aircraft, and defense applications. Signed a long-term development agreement with a leading construction and mining equipment OEM to integrate IRIS lidar into next-generation autonomous hauling vehicles, and bridge to integration of the Company's next-gen HALO lidar. Fulfilled increasing demand for active evaluations with customers spanning target markets, including with a leading AI company and hyperscaler for robotics and autonomous systems, a leading e-commerce company for aerial logistics and delivery, a defense contractor for mission-ready ground autonomy, and more. Shipped IRIS and MOVIA sensors supporting customer programs across industrial automation, autonomous systems, aerospace, defense, and artificial intelligence applications. Launched MicroVision Semiconductor , establishing an in-house semiconductor organization that expands the Company's custom ASIC, mixed-signal IC and advanced imaging capabilities while supporting both internal product development and external customer programs. Strengthened the executive leadership team with the appointments of James Byun as Chief Commercial Officer and Cara Klaer as Head of Marketing & Communications. Improved full-year cash burn guidance to approximately $60 million, reflecting expected normalization in the second half of the year following non-recurring cash usage in the first half, with improvement due to continued operational discipline and acquisition synergies. Completed a 1-for-15 reverse stock split , strengthening the Company's capital markets position and supporting continued Nasdaq listing compliance. "Our second quarter demonstrates that MicroVision has evolved into a commercially focused perception company with the products, technology, leadership and operational discipline needed to compete across multiple high-growth markets," said Glen DeVos, Chief Executive Officer of MicroVision. "Our Lidar 2.0 strategy is translating into meaningful commercial momentum and a path to near-term and future revenue." "Our strategy is simple: deliver the right perception solutions at the right cost across multiple industries. We're leveraging a common technology platform to address opportunities spanning industrial automation, security and defense, autonomous aerial systems, robotics and automotive. Every new customer, product and market reinforces the scalability of our business model and the trajectory of our revenue growth." Key Financial Highlights for Q2 2026 Revenue for the second quarter of 2026 was $1.5 million, compared to $0.2 million for the second quarter of 2025, primarily as a result of a greater volume of sensors shipped, as well as development revenue, during the second quarter of 2026. Total operating expenses for the second quarter of 2026 were $24.9 million, compared to $14.1 million for the second quarter of 2025, with the increase primarily relating to costs stemming from the acquisitions, along with integration and consolidation activities, during the second quarter of 2026. Net loss for the second quarter of 2026 was $36.9 million, or $1.66 per share, compared to a net loss of $14.2 million, or $0.84 per share, for the second quarter of 2025. Per share amounts have been adjusted to reflect the 1-for-15 reverse stock split that became effective on August 1, 2026. Adjusted EBITDA for the second quarter of 2026 was a $18.8 million loss, compared to a $11.2 million loss for the second quarter of 2025. Cash used in operations in the second quarter of 2026 was $19.1 million, which includes non-recurring payments related to acquisition and consolidation activities, compared to cash used in operations in the second quarter of 2025 of $12.7 million. The Company ended the second quarter of 2026 with $27.2 million in cash and cash equivalents, including investment securities, compared to $74.8 million at December 31, 2025. As of June 30, 2026, the Company has access to $68.4 million of capital, subject to certain conditions, including $41.2 million under its existing ATM, or at-the-market, facility and expects future financing activities to support continued execution of its strategic plan. Conference Call MicroVision will host a conference call today at 4:30 p.m. Eastern Time to discuss second quarter 2026 financial results and provide a business update. The live webcast can be accessed on the Investor Relations section of the Company's website at www.microvision.com . A replay of the webcast will be available following the conclusion of the call. About MicroVision MicroVision is defining the next generation of lidar-based perception solutions for automotive, industrial, and security & defense markets. As the industry moves beyond proof of concept toward value, deployment, and commercialization, MicroVision delivers integrated hardware and software solutions designed for real-world performance, automotive-grade reliability, and economic scalability. With engineering centers in the U.S. and Germany, MicroVision leads the industry in depth and breadth of its portfolio, with both short- and long-range lidar solutions, featuring solid-state sensors with varying wavelengths, advanced sensor architectures, design-to-cost engineering, and open software solutions. For more information, visit the Company's website at www.microvision.com , on Facebook at www.facebook.com/microvisioninc , and LinkedIn at https://www.linkedin.com/company/microvision/ . MicroVision, MAVIN, MOSAIK, MOVIA, IRIS, and SENTINEL are trademarks of MicroVision, Inc. in the United States and other countries. All other trademarks are the properties of their respective owners. Non-GAAP Information To supplement MicroVision's condensed financial statements presented in accordance with GAAP, the Company presents investors with the non-GAAP financial measures "adjusted EBITDA" and "adjusted Gross Profit." Adjusted EBITDA consists of GAAP net income (loss) excluding the impact of the following: interest income and interest expense; income tax expense; depreciation and amortization; non-cash gains and losses; share-based compensation; restructuring costs; severance expense; and impairment charges. Adjusted Gross Profit is calculated as GAAP gross profit before share-based compensation expense and the amortization of acquired intangibles included in cost of revenue. MicroVision believes that the presentation of adjusted EBITDA and adjusted Gross Profit provides important supplemental information to management and investors regarding financial and business trends, provides consistency and comparability with MicroVision's past financial reports, and facilitates comparisons with other companies in the Company's industry, many of which use similar non-GAAP financial measures to supplement their GAAP results. Internally, management uses these non-GAAP measures when evaluating operating performance because the exclusion of the items described above provides an additional useful measure of the Company's operating results and facilitates comparisons of the Company's core operating performance against prior periods and its business objectives. Externally, the Company believes that adjusted EBITDA and adjusted Gross Profit are useful to investors in their assessment of MicroVision's operating performance and the valuation of the Company. Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted Gross Profit are not calculated in accordance with GAAP, and should be considered supplemental to, and not as a substitute for, or superior to, financial measures calculated in accordance with GAAP. Non-GAAP financial measures have limitations in that they do not reflect all of the costs associated with the operations of MicroVision's business as determined in accordance with GAAP. The Company expects to continue to incur expenses similar to the non-GAAP adjustments described above, and exclusion of these items from its non-GAAP financial measures should not be construed as an inference that these costs are unusual or infrequent. The Company compensates for limitations of the adjusted EBITDA measure by prominently disclosing GAAP net income (loss), which the Company believes is the most directly comparable GAAP measure, and providing investors with a reconciliation from GAAP net income (loss) to adjusted EBITDA. Similarly for adjusted Gross Profit, the Company compensates for limitations of the measure by prominently disclosing GAAP gross profit which is the difference between Revenue and Cost of revenue, which the Company believes is the most directly comparable GAAP measure, and providing investors with a reconciliation by backing out share-based compensation expense and the amortization of acquired intangibles included in cost of revenue. Forward-Looking Statements Certain statements contained in this release, including market position, expectations, and likelihood of success; opportunities for customer engagement and revenue; expense reduction; benefits of acquisitions and integration synergies; market position; product portfolio; product and manufacturing capabilities; transaction benefits; access to capital and capital-raising opportunities; and expected revenue, expenses and cash usage are forward-looking statements that involve a number of risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those in the forward-looking statements. Factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those projected in such forward-looking statements include the risk its ability to operate with limited cash or to raise additional capital when needed; market acceptance of its technologies and products or for products incorporating its technologies; the failure of its commercial partners to perform as expected under its agreements; its financial and technical resources relative to those of its competitors; its ability to keep up with rapid technological change; government regulation of its technologies; its ability to enforce its intellectual property rights and protect its proprietary technologies; the ability to obtain customers and develop partnership opportunities; the timing of commercial product launches and delays in product development; the ability to achieve key technical milestones in key products; dependence on third parties to develop, manufacture, sell and market its products; potential product liability claims; its ability to maintain its listing on The Nasdaq Stock Market, and other risk factors identified from time to time in the Company's SEC reports, including the Company's Annual Report on Form 10-K, Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q and other reports filed with the SEC. These factors are not intended to represent a complete list of the general or specific factors that may affect the Company. It should be recognized that other factors, including general economic factors and business strategies, may be significant, now or in the future, and the factors set forth in this release may affect the Company to a greater extent than indicated. Except as expressly required by federal securities laws, the Company undertakes no obligation to publicly update or revise any forward-looking statements, whether as a result of new information, future events, changes in circumstances or any other reason. title: ZoomInfo pricing and reviews (2026)
summary: What ZoomInfo costs in 2026, its gated tiers and entry estimate, the go-to-market intelligence repositioning, honest reviewer themes, and fit.
body_text: ZoomInfo does not publish prices. It is gated B2B data software sold on annual contracts, and buyers report entry deals from roughly $15,000 a year, climbing well into six figures with more seats, credits, and modules. It now positions itself as a go-to-market (GTM) intelligence platform and trades under the ticker GTM. Reviewers praise the US data depth and criticize the contract terms. ZoomInfo pricing at a glance (2026) Plan What it covers Pricing (as of 2026) Professional Core contact and company data, search, basic exports Custom, contact sales (estimated from roughly $15,000/year) Advanced Adds intent data, WebSights visitor ID, deeper credits Custom, contact sales Elite Full platform, Scoops, advanced workflows and integrations Custom, contact sales Add-on modules Enrichment, engagement, data, operations, chat Custom, priced separately All figures are gated. The roughly $15,000 entry is a buyer-reported estimate, not a published rate, and it applies to a small deployment. Intent, visitor identification, engagement, and operations modules are typically separate line items, so the real cost depends heavily on which parts of the platform you buy. How much does ZoomInfo cost in practice? The entry estimate rarely resembles the signed deal. ZoomInfo pricing scales with the number of seats, the credits you consume for exports and enrichment, and the modules you add on top of core data, intent, visitor identification, engagement, operations, and data management. A team that starts with core Professional data and later adds intent and WebSights can see the contract multiply. Larger enterprise deployments run well into six figures a year. Credits are the variable that catches teams out. Data access is metered, and heavy exporting or enrichment can exhaust a credit balance and trigger overage conversations mid-contract. On top of the license, budget for the internal work of integrating ZoomInfo with your CRM and keeping data hygiene in check, since even the best B2B database decays. The fully loaded cost is the license plus credits plus the modules plus the operational upkeep. What do the ZoomInfo tiers include? The tiers step up along data breadth, intent, and workflow depth. Professional covers core contact and company data with search and exports, the foundation most buyers start on. Advanced layers in intent data and WebSights, ZoomInfo's website visitor identification. Elite opens the fullest platform, including Scoops (ZoomInfo's sourced sales and org intelligence) and advanced workflows and integrations. Around those core tiers sit the add-on modules that reflect the go-to-market intelligence repositioning: enrichment and operations tools, an engagement layer, and chat. This is where the positioning shows its shape. ZoomInfo is a data platform first, and execution capability is built out through modules you buy on top. The more of that stack you assemble, the closer it comes to an all-in-one, and the larger the contract. What are the hidden costs of ZoomInfo? The costs buyers most often underestimate are credit overages, add-on modules, and the contract and renewal terms. ZoomInfo's paperwork has a reputation among buyers, so read the auto-renewal, term length, and true-up clauses carefully before signing, and negotiate them explicitly. Because pricing is opaque and negotiated, comparable companies do not always pay comparable rates, which makes bargaining power a real cost factor. There is also the data-decay tax. B2B contact data goes stale, so part of ZoomInfo's value depends on continuous refresh and on your team maintaining hygiene in your CRM. And because execution lives in add-on modules, teams that want to act on the data, not just access it, end up buying more of the platform or pairing ZoomInfo with separate engagement tools. Either way, the data license is the beginning of the spend, not the end. For the wider category, see the best B2B data providers and the best email and phone number finder tools for sales . What do reviewers say about ZoomInfo? The consensus is that ZoomInfo is the enterprise standard for US B2B data depth. Reviewers report that the contact and company coverage, especially in the US, is among the best available, that WebSights and Scoops are useful, and that integrations with major CRMs are strong. For teams that depend on data breadth and accuracy in the US market, the coverage is a genuine strength. The criticisms are consistent and pointed. Reviewers report that pricing is high and opaque, that data can decay and accuracy varies (especially outside the US), and that contract and renewal terms, including auto-renewal, draw frequent complaints. Some describe the sales process as aggressive. The balanced read is straightforward. The US data holds up, the product is priced and contracted like the enterprise incumbent it is, and execution arrives as an add-on rather than the core. Who is ZoomInfo best for, and not for? ZoomInfo best fits mid-market and enterprise teams that need deep, reliable US B2B data at scale, with the budget for an annual contract and the operations function to integrate it and maintain hygiene. If your motion depends on the broadest, most accurate US contact and company coverage, it is a category leader. It fits less well for small teams and for buyers focused on EMEA or heavily international data, where coverage and privacy rules narrow the advantage. It also fits less well for teams that want one system to both hold the data and run the outreach. ZoomInfo is a data platform first. Execution comes through modules or separate tools. If your bottleneck is acting on data rather than accessing it, weigh the full stack cost, not just the data license. Worth considering: Artisan If you are evaluating ZoomInfo because you need data to drive outbound, it is worth looking at a system where the data and the activation live together and the AI does the acting. ZoomInfo gives you the database and a set of modules to bolt execution on. Artisan pairs a large contact database with the outreach and runs it, so you are not buying data in one place and a way to act on it in another. See Artisan vs. ZoomInfo . Ava, Artisan's AI business development representative (BDR), sources best-fit leads from a database of over 250 million B2B professionals across over 200 countries, plus Artisan Local Data with over 250 million local businesses, enriches them with waterfall email and phone enrichment (charged only on success), and prioritizes by conversion likelihood. Then she runs the motion: personalized multichannel campaigns across email, social media, and the dialer, reply and objection handling from a knowledge base, and meeting booking with CRM-owner routing. Signals like funding rounds, newly hired executives, active hiring, tech-stack intent, Bombora-powered topic intent, champion job changes, and person-level website visitor identification feed the campaigns automatically. You can also define your own signals in plain English, with confidence scoring and evidence URLs on the results. It runs on an autonomy dial with plain-language escalation and a full audit trail, and Artisan is SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, and CCPA compliant. The pricing model is the contrast that matters. Ava's work runs on usage-based credits, so you pay for the work she actually performs rather than signing a large annual data contract with metered credits, and there is a free trial with no auto-renewing seat lock-in to negotiate. Dialer seats and phone numbers are billed separately, at $75/seat/month when paid monthly. See Artisan pricing . SaaStr, an Artisan customer, sent 6,892 emails through Ava in about six weeks, 3,574 of them to new leads, and recorded a 3.6% positive response rate alongside 49.4% acceptance on social media connection requests. For a team weighing ZoomInfo, the question is whether you need the deepest US data to hand to your reps, or a system that has the data and runs the outbound itself. FAQ How much does ZoomInfo cost? ZoomInfo does not publish pricing. Its Professional, Advanced, and Elite plans are gated and quoted per deal on annual contracts. Buyers report an entry point from roughly $15,000 a year for a small deployment, climbing well into six figures as seats, credits, and add-on modules increase. Treat any figure as a buyer-reported estimate, not a published rate, until you have a quote. Why is ZoomInfo so expensive? ZoomInfo prices as the enterprise data incumbent: a seat-and-credit license for core data, plus separate modules for intent, visitor identification, engagement, and operations. The more of the platform you assemble, the higher the contract. Its US data depth commands a premium, and pricing is negotiated rather than public, so the cost depends heavily on configuration and bargaining power. Did ZoomInfo rebrand? Not as a legal name change. ZoomInfo has repositioned itself as a go-to-market intelligence platform, and its Nasdaq ticker changed from ZI to GTM in May 2025. The company name is still ZoomInfo. The positioning reflects its push beyond a data provider into modules for intent, engagement, and operations layered on the core database. How accurate is ZoomInfo's data? Reviewers consistently rate ZoomInfo's US contact and company data among the best in the market. Accuracy is strongest in the US and can vary internationally, and like all B2B databases it decays, so continuous refresh and CRM hygiene matter. Its claim of over 321M profiles is a marketing figure, while investor filings have historically cited over 235M. What should I watch for in a ZoomInfo contract? Read the auto-renewal, term length, credit limits, and true-up clauses closely. ZoomInfo's contract and renewal terms draw frequent buyer complaints, so negotiate them explicitly up front. Also clarify which modules are included versus add-ons, and how credit overages are handled, since those are the line items that most often push the real cost above the quoted figure. What are alternatives to ZoomInfo? For accessible all-in-one data, Apollo publishes per-seat pricing (free to $119/user/month). For EMEA compliance depth, Cognism is a gated leader. For a system that pairs a large contact database with AI-run outbound rather than data plus separate execution modules, Artisan runs Ava's work on usage-based credits with a free trial and bills dialer seats separately. See also the best ZoomInfo alternatives , ZoomInfo vs. Apollo , the best People Data Labs alternatives , and the best LeadIQ alternatives . Compare the category on our 6sense pricing and reviews page, see what an AI BDR does with contact data, or explore Artisan's AI sales agent and pricing . title: Infant & Baby Tylenol Dosage by Weight (Pediatrician's Chart)
summary: Board-certified pediatrician's weight-based Tylenol dosing chart for infants and babies. Safe amounts, timing, and when to call your doctor. Updated 2026.
body_text: Infant Tylenol is generally safe for babies 3 months and older who weigh at least 12 pounds. Give 10 to 15 mg per kilogram of body weight, every 4 hours as needed. Do not exceed 5 doses in 24 hours. Under 3 months, any fever needs pediatric evaluation before any medication. Use the weight-based chart below to find the right amount for your baby. In our telehealth visits, "How much Tylenol can I give my baby?" is one of the most common late-night messages we get. Below, a pediatrician walks you through the exact dose by weight, how to give it safely, and when to call your doctor instead. Not sure about the right dose for your baby? Talk to a pediatrician Key Takeaways Give 10 to 15 mg per kilogram of your baby's weight, every 4 hours as needed. Always dose by weight, not by age. Give no more than 5 doses in any 24-hour period. Do not give Tylenol at home to a baby under 3 months. Call your pediatrician first. Infant and Children's Tylenol are the same strength (160 mg per 5 mL). Use the oral syringe that comes in the box. Never a kitchen spoon. Call Poison Help (1-800-222-1222) right away if you think you gave too much. What Is Baby Tylenol (Infant Acetaminophen)? Baby Tylenol is a brand-name pain reliever and fever reducer for infants and children. Its active ingredient is acetaminophen (also called paracetamol outside the U.S.). Acetaminophen is one of the most-studied medicines in pediatrics. It lowers fever and eases mild to moderate pain. It is sold over the counter without a prescription. "Tylenol" is the best-known brand, but generic store-brand acetaminophen works just as well. The FDA requires generics to have the same active ingredient at the same concentration. There is no difference in safety or effectiveness. Parents most often use baby Tylenol for fever, teething pain, post-vaccine fussiness, and pain from ear infections. It comes as a flavored liquid, measured with an oral syringe. For a fuller walkthrough of fever itself — from taking a temperature to knowing when it's an emergency — see our baby fever guide . When Can You Give a Baby Tylenol? Acetaminophen is generally safe for babies 3 months (12 weeks) and older, at the right weight-based dose. Under 3 months, do not give it at home. Under 12 weeks Do not dose at home. Call your pediatrician immediately. The American Academy of Pediatrics does not publish a home Tylenol dose for babies under 3 months. Any fever of 100.4°F or higher (taken rectally) in a baby this young may signal a serious infection and needs medical evaluation, not fever medicine at home. Most pediatricians follow these guidelines: Age minimum: 12 weeks (3 months). For any fever in a baby under 3 months, call your pediatrician right away. Post-vaccine exception: Some pediatricians may recommend acetaminophen for babies as young as 8 weeks after their shots. Give it only when your pediatrician directs it, and at the exact dose they specify. Common uses: Fever, teething pain, post-vaccine soreness, and pain from ear infections. When not to give: Babies under 12 weeks (without doctor guidance), children with known liver disease, or anyone with an allergy to acetaminophen. Do not give acetaminophen before a vaccine as a preventive step. Studies show this can lower the immune response to the vaccine. Only give it after, and only if your baby seems uncomfortable. Infant Tylenol Dosage by Weight The right dose depends on your child's weight, not age. Use weight when you know it. Fall back to age only if you do not. "Weight-based dosing is the medical standard for safety," says Dr. Melissa Tribuzio, MD, a board-certified pediatrician at Blueberry Pediatrics. "A big 4-month-old and a small 8-month-old should not get the same amount." The standard strength for all infant and children's liquid acetaminophen is 160 mg per 5 mL. This has been the single standardized concentration since the FDA phased out the old, more concentrated infant drops in 2011. Weight (lbs) Weight (kg) Age range Liquid (160 mg / 5 mL) Chewable tablets (160 mg) 6 to 11 lbs 2.7 to 5.0 kg 0 to 3 months Under pediatrician direction only — do not dose at home N/A 12 to 17 lbs 5.4 to 7.7 kg 3 to 11 months 2.5 mL N/A 18 to 23 lbs 8.2 to 10.4 kg 12 to 23 months 3.75 mL N/A 24 to 35 lbs 10.9 to 15.9 kg 2 to 3 years 5 mL 1 tablet 36 to 47 lbs 16.3 to 21.3 kg 4 to 5 years 7.5 mL 1.5 tablets 48 to 59 lbs 21.8 to 26.8 kg 6 to 8 years 10 mL 2 tablets 60 to 71 lbs 27.2 to 32.2 kg 9 to 10 years 12.5 mL 2.5 tablets 72 to 95 lbs 32.7 to 43.1 kg 11 years 15 mL 3 tablets Chewable tablets carry a choking risk for younger children. Only give a chewable if your child can chew and swallow solid food; otherwise, use the liquid. For babies under 12 weeks or under 6 lbs, call your pediatrician before giving any acetaminophen. Not sure about the right dose? Message a pediatrician How to Give Baby Tylenol Safely Giving the right dose matters, but so does giving it the right way. Follow these steps every time. Use the oral syringe that comes with the product. Studies show syringes are more accurate than dosing cups for liquid medicine. Skip kitchen spoons. Teaspoons and tablespoons are not precise enough and can lead to dosing errors. Aim for the cheek. Squirt the liquid slowly toward the inside of your baby's cheek, not straight to the back of the throat. This helps prevent gagging. Wait at least 4 hours between doses. Never give more than 5 doses in 24 hours. Check other medicines for hidden acetaminophen. Many cold, flu, and cough products already contain it. Doubling up can lead to an overdose. Store between 68 and 77°F. Check the expiration date before each use. Keep it out of reach. A child-resistant cap is not a substitute for safe storage. How Often Can I Give My Baby Tylenol? You can give Tylenol every 4 hours as needed, up to a maximum of 5 doses in any 24-hour period. Do not exceed either limit. This dose, interval, and 24-hour cap come directly from the AAP and FDA labeling for infant and children's acetaminophen. Sticking to the schedule protects your baby's liver, which is where acetaminophen is broken down. If fever or pain is not controlled between doses, call your pediatrician before you give an extra dose or switch to another medicine. Do not double up on a missed dose. Not sure it's actually a fever? Our normal baby temperature guide covers the numbers by measurement method. Infant Tylenol vs. Children's Tylenol: What's the Difference? Infant Tylenol and Children's Tylenol are the exact same medicine at the exact same strength (160 mg per 5 mL). The only real difference is the measuring device in the box. Infant Tylenol comes with an oral syringe for smaller, more precise doses. Children's Tylenol comes with a dosing cup. That is why Infant Tylenol often costs 2 to 3 times more per ounce. You are paying for the syringe, not a stronger formula. Before 2011, infant drops were about 3 times more concentrated than children's liquid. Parents accidentally switching between products caused dangerous overdoses. The FDA standardized both to 160 mg per 5 mL to prevent these mistakes. If you only have Children's Tylenol at home, you can safely use it for your infant. Measure with an oral syringe and dose by weight using the chart above. Ask your pediatrician if you are unsure. Can You Alternate Tylenol and Motrin (Ibuprofen)? No, not on your own. The AAP recommends using a single medicine (either acetaminophen or ibuprofen) for a given fever, not routinely alternating them. Two reasons drive that recommendation: Alternating raises the chance of dosing errors. That means giving the wrong medicine, giving it too soon, or doubling up. The most common driver of alternating-regimen calls to Poison Control is caregiver dosing confusion, not the medicine itself. The temperature benefit is small. AAP guidance notes that alternating regimens can lower fever slightly more than a single medicine, but comfort and parent confidence, not the exact number on the thermometer, are the right outcomes at home. Alternate only when your pediatrician has told you to and has written down a schedule. If they do: Remember ibuprofen (Motrin) is not safe for babies under 6 months. Only acetaminophen is an option below that age. Keep a written log of which medicine you gave and when. Do not alternate for more than 24 hours without checking back with your doctor. Signs of Overdose and When to Call Poison Control Call Poison Help right away if you think you gave too much Tylenol, even if your baby looks fine. Early acetaminophen overdose often has no symptoms. If in doubt, call Poison Help 1-800-222-1222. This line is free, confidential, and open 24 / 7. It is answered by nurses, pharmacists, and toxicologists. Call before you drive to the ER so they can tell you exactly what to do. Do not wait for symptoms. Early overdose can look completely normal. The tricky part of acetaminophen overdose is that liver injury can take a day or more to show. Watch for these signs and call your pediatrician or Poison Help if you see them: First 24 hours: Often no symptoms, or mild nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, or sweating. 1 to 2 days after: Nausea and vomiting may ease, but pain in the upper right belly, unusual sleepiness, or poor feeding can point to liver strain. After 2 days: Yellow tint to the skin or whites of the eyes (jaundice), extreme sleepiness, confusion, or a baby who is hard to wake. Poison Help can walk you through what to do in real time. They will tell you if your baby needs to be seen in an emergency room. In our practice, we ask parents to call them first for any suspected overdose. Do not wait. When to Call Your Pediatrician Call your pediatrician (or start a telehealth visit) if any of these apply: Your baby is under 3 months old and has any fever at all (100.4°F or higher, taken rectally). Fever lasts more than 24 hours in a baby 3 to 24 months, or more than 3 days in a child 2 or older. Your baby seems very fussy, extra sleepy, is not drinking, or has fewer wet diapers than usual. Fever is 104°F or higher at any age. You are not sure of the right dose for your baby's weight. If you gave too much Tylenol, call Poison Help (1-800-222-1222) first, then your pediatrician. For fever specifically in a baby under 3 months, our newborn fever guide walks through the age-based worry thresholds. Fever or dosing worry that will not wait? Start a visit How Blueberry Pediatrics can help A sick baby at 2 a.m. is stressful, especially when you are staring at a bottle and doing kilogram math in your head. Blueberry Pediatrics gives you around-the-clock access to board-certified pediatricians by message, phone, and video. We can confirm the right dose for your baby's weight and tell you if a fever needs to be seen. And we can answer the second question you did not know you had yet. You do not have to guess alone. FAQ How much Tylenol can I give my baby? The dose is 10 to 15 mg per kilogram of your baby's weight. Give it every 4 hours as needed, up to 5 doses in 24 hours. See the chart above for the exact mL amount. Always dose by weight when you know it. Can I give my newborn Tylenol? No. Do not give Tylenol at home to a baby under 3 months. The AAP does not publish a home dose for this age. Any fever in a baby under 3 months needs medical evaluation right away, not fever medicine at home. How often can I give my baby Tylenol? Every 4 hours as needed, and no more than 5 doses in any 24-hour period. Do not give an earlier or extra dose without calling your pediatrician first. Can I give Tylenol without a fever? Yes, if your baby is 3 months or older and clearly uncomfortable from teething, an ear infection, or post-vaccine soreness. The weight-based dose is the same as for fever. What's the difference between Infant Tylenol and Children's Tylenol? Same medicine, same strength (160 mg per 5 mL) since 2011. The only difference is the measuring device. Infant Tylenol comes with a syringe. Children's Tylenol comes with a dosing cup. What if I gave too much Tylenol to my baby? Call Poison Help right away at 1-800-222-1222. Do not wait for symptoms. Early overdose can look normal, and calling early gives your baby the best outcome. Can I give my baby Tylenol and Motrin together? Not on your own. The AAP recommends a single medicine for a given fever. Alternate only if your pediatrician has told you to and written down a schedule. What are the signs of Tylenol overdose in babies? Early overdose often has no symptoms. Later signs can include vomiting, upper-right belly pain, extreme sleepiness, poor feeding, or a yellow tint to the skin or whites of the eyes. How much Tylenol for a 2-month-old? Do not give Tylenol at home to a baby under 3 months. Call your pediatrician first. How much Tylenol for a 4-month-old? For a baby 12 to 17 lbs, give 2.5 mL of the 160 mg / 5 mL liquid. Confirm with your baby's actual weight. How much Tylenol for a 6-month-old? Dose by weight, not age. A 6-month-old commonly weighs 14 to 18 lbs — babies at 12 to 17 lbs take 2.5 mL, and babies at 18 to 23 lbs take 3.75 mL. See the chart above for your baby's exact weight. How long does infant Tylenol take to work? Usually 30 to 60 minutes to lower a fever or ease pain. If your baby is not more comfortable at that point, call your pediatrician before adding another dose. What if my baby spits out the Tylenol? If most of it came out within a few minutes, you can give the full dose again. If your baby swallowed part of it or vomited well after taking it, call your pediatrician or Poison Help before re-dosing. Is generic acetaminophen as good as brand-name Tylenol? Yes. The FDA requires generics to have the same active ingredient at the same strength. Generic infant acetaminophen works exactly like brand-name Tylenol at a lower price. Sources American Academy of Pediatrics. Acetaminophen (Tylenol) Pictographic Dosing Chart (PDF) . U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Important change in concentration for OTC liquid acetaminophen marketed for infants . America's Poison Centers / Poison Help. 1-800-222-1222: the national Poison Help line . Agrawal S, Khazaeni B. Acetaminophen Toxicity . StatPearls [Internet]. NCBI Bookshelf NBK441917 (revised 2024).
